page: Microsoft Azure D8als_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine belonging to the low-memory variant of the general-purpose Dalsv7 series. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. System memory is configured at 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector and matrix extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

No bundled local storage is included on the instance, relying instead on remote Azure premium storage volumes for persistent IOPS and disk needs. The instance also features zero local GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC architecture exhibits top-tier single-core performance, scoring in the top 10% on stress-ng and achieving 40.84 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-core compute performance and uncached memory throughput sit within median percentiles, with large block uncached read bandwidth registering at 49.0 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 33.7 GB/sec.

With its 2 GB per vCPU distribution, the instance provides cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools. The primary architectural tradeoff is the restricted memory footprint and lack of native ephemeral storage. D8als_v7 is well suited for batch compute processing, microservices, front-end web serving, continuous integration runners, and lightweight compression workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D8als_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine optimized with a reduced memory profile. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, the instance delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs over 4 physical cores and includes 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The CPU architecture includes AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic instruction extensions, backed by a 32 MB L3 cache. There is no bundled local ephemeral storage and no GPU acceleration, necessitating external Azure managed disks for file storage. Benchmark metrics emphasize top-decile single-core CPU throughput and compression rates, accompanied by balanced multi-core and memory subsystem performance. D8als_v7 represents an economical compute tier for CPU-centric processing, continuous integration build jobs, web serving, and lightweight container deployments where large memory allocations are unnecessary.
